answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a bonded stake in a shared vault before it can grade or attest anything. A cheap swarm of fake identities then has to lock up real capital for each seat it wants, so mass registration becomes expensive. The stake is slashed when peers prove an agent attested to a bad answer, which makes a fresh voyage through the network costly for cheaters. Honest agents keep their bond and earn rewards over time. Reputation built from settled rounds, rather than from raw account count, is what the prism of trust should weigh.
